about.heading: About me
paragraphs: I'm Anton, a designer, developer and founder of KADO. I lead the key stages myself: understanding the brief, shaping the structure, setting the visual direction and making sure the idea becomes a working website. When a project needs a photographer, copywriter or 3D specialist, I bring them in for that task and make their roles clear.

Form matters, but a site also needs clear structure, an easy path to the right information and reliable behaviour across screens. The work moves from the brief and concept through design and development to checks before launch. I can stay involved with updates and further development afterwards.

blocks.title:
A space,
assembled into one
digital system.
paragraphs: For Audience, I carried the character of its interior and visual language into the structure of the site. This case study follows the composition, navigation and content-management decisions.
The challenge was to bring the concept, interior, cuisine and service together in one clear digital experience.

media.alt: Audience interior with guests seated at tables
Audience homepage with natural textures on a laptop

blocks.title: Visual language as part of navigation.
paragraphs: The visual system avoids decorative imitation of Eastern aesthetics. It is built on depth, natural textures, the contrast of light and shadow, open space and a restrained pace of interaction. These principles run consistently through every part of the website.
Navigation ties the concept, interior, menu and service together. The same structure supports three languages: Russian, English and Chinese.

media.alt: Mobile version of the Audience website on a smartphone held in one hand

blocks.title: How do you organize a complex content structure?

media.alt: Audience homepage with a waterfall image on a tablet

lead.text: Each menu section has its own structure of categories, cards and editorial content.

blocks.fillText: Each section has its own structure, categories, cards and content.

feature.alt: Samurai armour in the dark Audience interior

detail.alt: Audience main menu and green tea card on mobile screens

rows.statement: The main UX challenge was to keep the depth of the material while making the structure easy to understand.

feature.alt: Intimate Audience seating area with a low table and warm light

detail.alt: Audience menu section with a teapot photograph on a laptop

rows.statement: The information architecture and category system follow the same rules.

blocks.title:
Motion as part of
navigation.
paragraphs: Animation connects screens, marks transitions between sections and supports the reading order without turning into a spectacle.

media.alt: Audience homepage animation on a laptop surrounded by natural textures

blocks.title:
A living website,
not a one-off
launch.
blocks.text: The project was built as an evolving content system. Menus and seasonal items can be updated, news published, imagery changed and sections kept current without rebuilding the website by hand.

media.alt: Audience admin panel with integration and image settings
Mobile Audience content-management panel on a smartphone

blocks.text: For Audience, I developed the structure, visual system, interface, animation and content-management tools. This case study presents completed design and technical work and does not offer or promote the client's products.

closing.alt: Audience logo against the bar interior

blocks.title:
One store,
several business
models.
paragraphs: Keys Store brings together Steam and PlayStation games, digital subscriptions, and the buying and selling of Steam items. Behind one brand are different product types, selection rules, payment methods and user expectations.

media.alt: Keys Store cart with digital products and total price on a smartphone
Keys Store mobile interface in a still-life composition with dark stones

blocks.statement: The task was not to make yet another catalog. It was to create a commerce system where people immediately understand what they are buying, which platform it works on and how to complete the transaction.

blocks.title:
A shared language
for every catalog.
paragraphs: I created one language for every catalog: a shared grid, cards, filters, typographic hierarchy, statuses and price treatment. Across each section, the logic stays familiar.
The system adapts to the product: a game shows platform and delivery method, a subscription its term and contents, and a Steam item its availability, purchase price and sale price.

media.alt: Keys Store game catalog with search and filters on a laptop

blocks.title:
The differences remain visible.
The system stays coherent.
paragraphs: A shared style does not mean identical interfaces. Each catalog gets its own emphasis and only the information needed to make a decision in that specific journey.

media.alt: Keys Store mobile game catalog with cards and prices
Counter-Strike item catalog in the Keys Store mobile interface
PlayStation Plus subscription cards in the Keys Store mobile catalog
Team Fortress 2 item catalog on a smartphone

blocks.statement: Product complexity is not hidden behind decorative uniformity; it is translated into clear decision-making criteria.

blocks.title:
A path to purchase
without needless decisions.
paragraphs: Buying a digital product can involve platform, region, edition, payment method and delivery method. I turned these choices into a clear sequence, with the next step and final terms visible before confirmation.
Different checkout options do not turn the process into a maze of technical forks. The interface reveals available actions in sequence and keeps the order clear.

media.alt: Keys Store marketplace mobile interface on a smartphone held in one hand

blocks.title:
Trust is built
into the interface.
paragraphs: The design explains how each transaction works, shows availability and timing, tracks order status and makes the terms transparent, from choosing a product to receiving a game or a payout for a sale.

media.alt: Keys Store marketplace with items and transaction parameters on a tablet
Set of Keys Store mobile screens showing products, transactions and messages

blocks.title:
Identity is
part of the product.
paragraphs: The logo and visual language bring diverse areas together in one recognizable product. Vibrant game imagery distinguishes the categories, while the interface shell maintains a common rhythm.
Identity does not exist apart from UX: it helps people recognize areas, platforms and service types more quickly.

media.alt: Green and purple game controller with the Keys Store logo

blocks.text: Keys Store is a large commerce system where different digital products become one clear experience. The journey stays familiar even as the product, platform and transaction model change.

closing.alt: Keys Store branded Steam games banner on an outdoor display

baltika.summary: How I designed the interface and 3D system for a brand website.

headerMedia.alt: Baltika Brew — 3D bottle model in Blender

blocks.title:
The challenge and
the central object.
paragraphs: For Baltika Brew, I developed the brand website structure, visual concept and a set of 3D scenes. This case study follows the key decisions behind the digital interface.
The bottle model became the central object. It set the rules for composition, materials and interface behavior across the site.
To comply with Russian law, certain elements in the imagery and layouts shown in this case study have been concealed or replaced with neutral alternatives.

media.alt: Island with autumn trees in water, part of the Baltika Brew visual system
Baltika Brew website with a landscape composition on a monitor and smartphone

blocks.title:
The label as part of
the visual system.
paragraphs: I integrated the label artwork into the 3D model and connected it to the background scenes. This created a shared way to present the range.
Products were distinguished through color, imagery and scene parameters, while the navigation and page structure remained consistent.

media.alt: Baltika Brew homepage with a 3D bottle on a laptop

blocks.title:
Original imagery
for every product.
paragraphs: For each product, I selected an original photograph and built an individual scene. Color, texture and scale distinguish the screens, while the overall composition keeps the stories connected.

media.alt: Lake and coniferous islands in mist, an illustration for Baltika Brew
Red cliffs in evening light, an illustration for Baltika Brew
Trees reflected in pink water, an illustration for Baltika Brew
Island with an autumn forest in blue water, an illustration for Baltika Brew

blocks.statement: The photography distinguishes each screen while preserving the integrity of the visual system.

blocks.title:
Motion as part of
the interface.
paragraphs: Animation moves between states of the 3D scene and sequences the appearance of information. It supports navigation and guides attention through the composition.

media.alt: Animation of the rotating Baltika Brew 3D bottle model

blocks.title:
Reference material
without visual noise.
paragraphs: For a large body of reference material, I developed a clear typographic hierarchy and compact information modules.
Content follows a clear visual hierarchy, keeping the screen readable without competing with the main 3D scene.

media.alt: Baltika Brew mobile page with a bottle and landscape artwork on its label

blocks.title:
Editorial and
reference sections.
paragraphs: News and reference material share a common navigation system and a repeatable page structure. This case study treats the section as part of the website's information architecture.

media.alt: Baltika Brew information section on a tablet held in both hands

blocks.title:
Responsive
composition.
paragraphs: Wide screens use a horizontal composition with text and graphic elements distributed across the canvas.
On mobile, the same material becomes a sequential vertical structure while retaining its reading order.

media.alt: Responsive Baltika Brew page with a landscape composition on a tablet

blocks.text: For Baltika Brew, I developed the brand website's structure, visual system, 3D graphics and animation. This case study describes completed design and technical work and does not offer or promote alcoholic products.

closing.alt: Series of Baltika Brew 3D bottle models with different landscape labels

headerMedia.alt: SCHMIDT website displayed on a monitor

blocks.title:
A brand story
in a horizontal rhythm.
paragraphs: Instead of the familiar downward movement, users travel through the SCHMIDT website from left to right. Brand identity, editorial blocks and interface scenes become one continuous sequence.

media.alt: SCHMIDT horizontal website composition

blocks.statement: The horizontal route sets the pace of discovery and turns the landing page into a continuous trajectory. It is not an effect for effect's sake.

blocks.title:
Clarity in a still-life
composition.
paragraphs: Clear glass, grain, pearls and a fine golden line shape the website's visual vocabulary. Contrasting objects connect individual screens into one visual system.
Large typography and white space keep the composition clear and composed without making it sterile.

media.alt: SCHMIDT web typography featuring DIN Pro and a screen with a photograph of wheat

blocks.title:
The brand story
as the next scene.
paragraphs: Family history, heritage and values do not sit on a separate text page. They become part of the same spatial sequence, giving each fact weight and rhythm without interrupting the movement.

media.alt: SCHMIDT history section with an illustration on a laptop screen
Horizontal SCHMIDT website composition on a smartphone held in one hand

blocks.title:
Production as
a transparent process.
paragraphs: The section is divided into four numbered scenes. I developed a distinct object image for each while keeping the grid, typography and motion consistent.

media.alt: Scene 01 of the SCHMIDT production section with an ear of wheat
Scene 02 of the SCHMIDT production section with a transparent blue droplet
Scene 03 of the SCHMIDT production section with a dimensional splash of water
Scene 04 of the SCHMIDT production section with a silver sphere

blocks.statement: Four distinct images become one continuous visual journey.

blocks.title:
The range continues
through distinct journeys.
paragraphs: Every product receives its own screen with an individual composition, color accent and arrangement of content.
Shared grid and typographic rules hold the sections together, while varied layouts prevent mechanical repetition.

media.alt: SCHMIDT website pages and still-life composition on a monitor

blocks.title:
One rhythm.
Different screens.
paragraphs: On a wide screen, the story unfolds as a long horizontal composition. On narrow screens, the order of scenes remains while guidance becomes more explicit.
Responsive design is not about shrinking blocks, but about preserving the same rhythm of discovering the brand.

media.alt: SCHMIDT website pages on a laptop with horizontal navigation

blocks.text: For SCHMIDT, I created a distinctive website with cohesive art direction, a horizontal rhythm and interactive animation. Grid, typography and object imagery connect every section into one clear brand story.

closing.alt: Horizontal SCHMIDT homepage on an ultrawide monitor
